Command: Give firstborn clean animals to the priests
Summary: The command: Give firstborn clean animals to the priests (Numbers 18:17). The flesh of the firstborn clean animals belonged to the priests, as the wave breast and heave shoulder.
Commandment: Give firstborn clean animals to the priests, as prescribed in Numbers 18:17.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Redemption of the firstborn remembered that God spared Israel's firstborn in Egypt. The New Testament speaks of Jesus as the firstborn and of believers as redeemed, but does not continue the redemption payment as a Christian rite (Colossians 1:15-18; 1 Peter 1:18-19).
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: because the LORD slew all the firstborn in Egypt and spared Israel's, therefore the firstborn are his (Exodus 13:14-15).
Function: The flesh of the firstborn clean animals belonged to the priests, as the wave breast and heave shoulder — a ceremonial law of priestly provision. Its goal was to feed Aaron's house from the firstborn offerings, the priests eating what belonged to the LORD. It did not address a particular evil; its work was provision and remembrance, not restraint. The firstborn that remembered Egypt also fed the men who served at the altar, and the memory and the meal went together.
